name: Call Christmas Tree Butterfly (1-3-2)
summary: Buy 1 call at A, sell 3 calls at B, buy 2 calls at C with equal strike spacing; a balanced but heavily unbalanced-ratio butterfly that widens the profit tent upward compared to a 1-2-1 fly.

legs.strike_rule: A = strike nearest ATM, call delta 0.45-0.55
B = A + W where W = 1.0-1.5% of spot; B delta 0.25-0.35
C = B + W (identical spacing); C delta 0.12-0.20

net: debit (usually a small one) or occasionally flat/credit
when_to_use: IV rank > 35, a slow uptrend, and call skew flat enough that selling 3 at B pays for the 1 at A and 2 at C. Contract count nets to zero (1 - 3 + 2 = 0), so the structure is fully defined-risk and Level 3 eligible.
max_profit: (W x 100) - net debit, at strike B
max_loss: net debit paid on the downside; on the upside the position converges to (net debit) as well because the 2 long C calls reclaim the extra short at B. Worst case is a finish between B and C: max loss there is bounded by (W x 100) + net debit minus the recovery from the C longs - compute per-fill from the payoff table before submitting.
breakevens: lower breakeven = A + debit/100; upper breakeven between B and C, solved numerically from the 1-3-2 payoff

greeks.delta: positive at entry (+10 to +25 per unit)
greeks.theta: positive when spot is below B

entry_rules: Strike spacing A->B and B->C must be exactly equal; reject otherwise.
Contract ratio strictly 1:3:2 so the net contract count is zero (no naked shorts); anything else is a Level 4 structure.
Compute the full expiry payoff at A, B, C and 2W beyond C before submitting; reject if the worst point on that curve exceeds 1.5% of equity.
All three strikes: OI >= 500, per-leg spread <= max($0.05, 10% of mid).
Single 6-contract multi-leg order at mid, pay up to mid + $0.04.
management_rules: Close at 30% of max profit, i.e. when mark >= debit + 0.30 x ((W x 100) - debit).
Close at 21 DTE regardless of P/L.
Close if spot trades above C - the tent has been exited on the upside.
Stop at 60% loss of the debit if spot falls below A.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: 3 short calls at B. Flatten by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close immediately if the B calls are ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close before the ex-date if the B calls are ITM with extrinsic below the declared dividend.
Close no later than 5 DTE; the 1-3-2 payoff between B and C is unforgiving at high gamma.
assignment_risk: Three short calls at B means -300 shares per unit on assignment, covered by only 1 long at A and 2 at C. If B is assigned while spot sits between B and C, the residual exposure is materially short. Highest assignment count of any structure in this family - treat the flatten rule as hard-wired.
buying_power: Net debit plus the broker's spread requirement on the 1-3-2 decomposition (typically one W-wide short call spread's width x 100 minus credit). Budget (W x 100) + debit per unit until the actual Alpaca margin response is observed.
liquidity_needs: High; six contracts per unit across three strikes.
common_mistakes: Using unequal strike spacing, which silently converts the structure into something with naked exposure; assuming it behaves like a 1-2-1 fly; ignoring the region between B and C where the payoff dips; holding to expiry with 3 short calls live.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended. Six contracts of slippage plus three short strikes to monitor into the close is a poor 0DTE risk/effort trade. If forced, treat it as intraday-only with a 15:45 ET flatten.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
bias_note: mildly bullish to neutral; profits if the underlying drifts up toward B
